items.title: George Shearing interviewed by Joe Williams, New York City, New York, March 8, 1996
items.q: Monk Rowe and Leslie Gourse participated briefly in the interview.

ctx.x: Pianist George Shearing was born in England on August 13, 1919. He received his first musical training at the Linden Lodge School for the Blind and his lack of sight proved no hindrance to an eventual career as a jazz pianist. He was recording by 1936 and quickly became a household name in England, being voted the top British pianist by Melody Maker from 1939-1946. His desire for a larger audience brought him to the U.S. in 1946 and his career has blossomed since then. George has performed and recorded solo, as…
George was interviewed by his good friend and frequent musical companion Joe Williams in New York City on March 8, 1996. Monk Rowe and Leslie Gourse participated briefly in the interview.

This is for the archives at Hamilton College. George, I’ve often wondered how an Englishman like you comes to the point you are with the music, and the legacy and the history of the music, and to understand it so well, and to go to innovations of your own from where you came from, relating to this music. How did you get to this music I want to know? The jazz, that good sound that you give us all over.
